terms.definition: One of the numbers you add together in an addition problem.
terms.function: Provides a group of items to be combined into the total.
terms.whereItIs: The two cube groups on the mat — 3 and 4.
terms.whyItMatters: Knowing the parts of addition helps you read and solve word problems.

terms.definition: The total result after the addends are combined.
terms.function: Answers the 'how many in all?' question.
terms.whyItMatters: The sum is the goal of every addition problem.

terms.definition: A strategy that starts at the first addend and counts forward the second addend's amount.
terms.function: Solves addition faster than counting every item from one.
terms.whereItIs: The arrow stepping along the number line.
terms.whyItMatters: It is one of the first mental-math shortcuts children learn.

terms.definition: Exchanging ten units of a place for one unit of the next higher place.
terms.function: Keeps column addition correct when a column reaches ten or more.
terms.whereItIs: The 'carry' step in the column view of the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the same place-value exchange that powers carrying in addition.

terms.definition: The property that changing the order of addends does not change the sum.
terms.whereItIs: Demonstrated by combining the two cube groups in either order.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets you add numbers in whatever order is easiest.
